task.name: forge triage: evidence-backed disposition proposals from a fixed taxonomy
task.story_text:
## What

The proposal stage of `forge triage`: for each finding in the backlog report, a fresh-context agent reads an evidence packet — the finding body, the deterministic staleness evidence from the report slice, and any per-run disposition history the audit substrate holds for it — and proposes exactly one disposition from a fixed taxonomy:

- `fix_now` (with a proposed current-milestone assignment)
- `fix_later` (with a proposed named milestone or the Hygiene standing pool)
- `punt` (with a reason code from the fixed set)
- `needs_verification` (evidence insufficient to decide)

This is the escalation advisor's shape applied to the backlog: evidence packet in, constrained schema-validated advisory out. Proposals are advisory only — nothing in this slice applies anything.

## Why

Slice 2 of epic #1033, blocked by the report slice. The three-outcome model is simple enough to automate the *proposal* step while keeping every decision with the operator. The constrained taxonomy is what makes proposals reviewable and auditable — free-form triage prose would be another unenforced guess.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every proposal is one of the fixed taxonomy values with its required payload (target milestone or pool for fix dispositions, reason code for punts). Schema-invalid agent output is rejected and retried; output that remains invalid resolves to `needs_verification` for that finding — never dropped, never guessed into a disposition.
- Every proposal cites evidence drawn from the packet it was given. A proposal resting on claims not present in the packet is rejected the same way schema-invalid output is.
- A finding whose packet contains no checkable evidence is proposed `needs_verification`, never `punt` — absence of evidence is not evidence for discard.
- The proposal stage performs no tracker writes of any kind on any issue.
- The run reports its spend: per-finding and total cost are visible in the output and written to the audit substrate, and an empty backlog spends nothing and says so.

## Example

```
#1312  PROPOSE punt (reason: verified-stale)
       evidence: report shows cited symbol absent from current tree;
       registry holds no disposition rows for this finding
#1124  PROPOSE fix_later → Hygiene (keep)
       evidence: cited file churned 11x since filing, finding text
       still matches; low blast radius (audit-count off-by-one)
#659   PROPOSE needs_verification
       evidence: no checkable artifact cited; cannot distinguish
       stale from active
```

## Non-goals

- No punt review, no operator interaction, no application — later slices.
- No automated (operator-skipping) mode; that is explicitly deferred out of the epic.

handoff.summary: Added the forge triage proposal stage: a fixed disposition taxonomy (fix_now/fix_later/punt/needs_verification) with per-disposition required payloads and a grounding rule, both enforced at a schema boundary in the new low-dependency theforge.triage_proposal module. theforge.triage_report defines the backlog-report contract the (not-yet-landed) report slice will produce, failing fast and legibly when the artifact is missing or malformed. theforge.task.triage_prompts renders the prompt from the taxonomy constants so it cannot drift from the validator. coordinator/triage_proposal_flow.py is pure-Python control flow: it builds one packet per finding (finding body + report evidence + this finding's own disposition history read back from the substrate), invokes a fresh agent via the reused advisor profile selector, retries once on schema-invalid or ungrounded output naming the validator's own errors, and falls back to needs_verification with the errors recorded; a packet with no checkable evidence resolves to needs_verification deterministically without invoking an agent, and an empty backlog selects no profile and invokes no runner. Two new substrate tables (triage_proposal_runs, triage_proposal_events) record per-finding proposals with packet hash, payload, cited evidence ids, validation errors, retry count, cost and cost provenance, plus a per-run spend summary including the explicit zero-cost empty-backlog run; SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 9 to 10 with a note that no re-index pass is implied. The forge triage CLI is a thin wrapper that prints one proposal per finding with per-finding and total spend and performs no tracker writes on any path.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every proposal is one of the fixed taxonomy values with its required payload (target milestone or pool for fix dispositions, reason code for punts). Schema-invalid agent output is rejected and retried; output that remains invalid resolves to needs_verification for that finding — never dropped, never guessed into a disposition.
acceptance_criteria.notes: parse_triage_proposal validates disposition membership and per-disposition payload (fix_now must equal the packet's current milestone; fix_later must be a named milestone or Hygiene; punt must carry a code from PUNT_REASON_CODES; needs_verification must carry neither). The flow retries once with the validator errors named in the prompt, then emits needs_verification with validation_errors and fallback_reason recorded. Tested including that a rejected punt never becomes a punt.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every proposal cites evidence drawn from the packet it was given. A proposal resting on claims not present in the packet is rejected the same way schema-invalid output is.
acceptance_criteria.notes: evidence_refs must be non-empty and every id must exist in the packet; unknown ids and missing evidence prose are rejected through the same parse_errors path, which drives the same retry-then-fallback.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A finding whose packet contains no checkable evidence is proposed needs_verification, never punt — absence of evidence is not evidence for discard.
acceptance_criteria.notes: FindingPacket.has_checkable_evidence gates the agent call entirely; the deterministic path uses needs_verification_proposal, the single constructor that can only produce needs_verification, at a measured $0.00. Report evidence entries default to checkable=False when the flag is absent, so an under-specified report routes here rather than to a discard.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The proposal stage performs no tracker writes of any kind on any issue.
acceptance_criteria.notes: No module in the change imports github_integration, subprocess, or any gh path. Pinned two ways: a static scan over all five triage modules, and runtime tests that fail if subprocess.run/Popen/check_output is called during a full flow run or a full CLI run.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The run reports its spend: per-finding and total cost are visible in the output and written to the audit substrate, and an empty backlog spends nothing and says so.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Per-finding cost and provenance render per proposal and a TOTAL SPEND line closes the run; both are written to triage_proposal_events and triage_proposal_runs. Unmeasured attempts render as 'unmeasured' and taint the run provenance rather than being zeroed. The empty backlog selects no profile, invokes no runner, prints an explicit $0.0000 message, and records a zero-cost run row.

story_deviations: The spec requires punt reason codes 'from the fixed set' but does not enumerate the set. Defined five codes (verified-stale, superseded, not-reproducible, duplicate, out-of-scope-by-policy) in a single module-level constant that the prompt renders from, so an authoritative enumeration from a later slice replaces one constant. Every code and rejection of unknown codes is tested.

fix_now requires a current milestone, and nothing in ForgeConfig supplies one. It comes from the report artifact's current_milestone or the --current-milestone flag; with neither, fix_now is removed from the packet's available dispositions and rejected by the validator rather than proposed against an unnameable target.

The report slice this story depends on has not landed, so this change defines the backlog-report contract itself in theforge/triage_report.py as an explicit adapter boundary. The command has no real input source until that slice is wired to this artifact shape; a missing or malformed artifact is an operator-legible error that invokes nothing.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixed both P1 findings. (1) Grounding validated evidence ids only, so a proposal could cite a real packet entry while asserting something the entry never said; citations are now {ref, quote} pairs where the quote must be a verbatim span of that specific entry's own text (case/punctuation-normalized, minimum MIN_QUOTE_WORDS=3 words), verified mechanically by _verify_quote. The free-text evidence field is gone entirely: TriageProposal.evidence is derived from the verified quotes, or from a coordinator-authored `basis` set only by needs_verification_proposal on the deterministic fallback paths. Agent prose now lands in `rationale`, rendered as 'reasoning (unverified)' below the evidence line and never merged into it. The prompt renders the quoting rule, the minimum length, and a packet-derived valid example from the same constants the validator enforces. (2) The proposer was dispatched with the selected model's own tool surface, in the project checkout, with the full secrets map, so the no-tracker-writes property rested on the prompt. Every invocation now passes through seal_proposer_profile() (allowed_tools set — not filtered — to the new config.TRIAGE_PROPOSER_TOOLS read-only, shell-free surface; sandbox_mode=read-only; phase/name stamped for the audit trail) and proposer_secrets() (an allowlist passing provider API keys only), and runs in an empty tempfile scratch directory removed when the run ends, never config.project_root.

fix_now requires a current milestone and nothing in ForgeConfig supplies one. It comes from the report artifact or --current-milestone; with neither, fix_now is removed from the packet's available dispositions and rejected by the validator rather than proposed against an unnameable target.

That is deliberately strict: a proposer that will not quote its packet gets retried once and then resolves to needs_verification, which is the safe direction. plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan's first stated risk is carried: Step 2 depends on a backlog-report artifact whose module, parser, finding identity, evidence fields, and history representation do not exist in the tree. A narrow adapter that merely fails clearly does not define the required data flow, including how existing per-run finding dispositions in audit_records.raw_json are matched to report findings. The analogous src/theforge/coordinator/escalation_advisor_flow.py:324 operates on concrete CoordinatorState and TaskStory APIs and cannot supply this missing contract.
  Suggestion: Make the landed report slice an explicit implementation dependency, then revise Step 2 to name its real parser/type and map each concrete report field and stable finding identifier into the packet and existing audit-history query.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan's second stated risk is carried on an acceptance-criterion surface. Step 1 permits inventing a minimal example-backed punt reason set, but the specification requires codes from a fixed set and does not enumerate that set. The example's verified-stale value is evidence of one member, not an authoritative complete taxonomy.
  Suggestion: Obtain or define the authoritative punt reason-code enumeration before implementation, place it at the schema boundary, and test every allowed code plus rejection of unknown codes.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 1 and 2 require fix_now to target the current milestone but never put the current milestone or permitted future milestones into the packet or CLI inputs. ForgeConfig has no project-current-milestone field at src/theforge/config/types.py:1371; its only nearby milestone setting is unrelated advisory issue-filing configuration at line 1330. The agent therefore cannot reliably propose, and the validator cannot enforce, a current-milestone assignment.
  Suggestion: Extend the report contract or command inputs with an authoritative current milestone and eligible named milestones, include them in every packet, and validate fix_now and fix_later targets against those values.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 1 (report slice absent). The plan's own risk list is correct: nothing in the tree produces a backlog findings report with per-finding staleness evidence (src/theforge/finding_fate_proxy/report.py and structural_decay_observer/report.py are the nearest analogues, neither is the declared input). The mitigation — a narrow report adapter plus a fail-fast CLI error — retires the 'predictably fails' concern and keeps every AC testable against constructed findings, but it means the shipped command has no real input source until the report slice lands, and the adapter's field contract is invented by this story.
  Suggestion: Define the adapter as an explicit dataclass/protocol at one module boundary (finding id, issue ref, body, evidence entries with stable IDs) so the report slice can be wired to it later without touching taxonomy/validation code, and make the missing-artifact path an operator-legible error with a test.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 adds new substrate tables but says nothing about SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 9 in src/theforge/coordinator/audit_storage.py:109) or the re-index pass a bump implies. tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py and the storage/read-model boundary guard (tests/test_audit_storage_read_model_boundary.py) will police this.
  Suggestion: Bump SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION with the new CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS blocks in _SCHEMA, keep writers in audit_storage.py and the prior-proposal SELECT helper in audit_read_model.py (storage must not import the read model), and re-export the new names from the audit_substrate facade. If the per-run record's serialized shape is unchanged, CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION and MIGRATION_HELPERS need no entry.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 says to invoke the advisor 'using the existing runner pattern from escalation_advisor_flow.run_escalation_advisor'. That function's signature is (state: CoordinatorState, config: ForgeConfig, task: TaskStory, workspace_path: Path) and it mutates state.advisory_*, selects a preflight profile, and prepares a baseline checkout via _prepare_preflight_working_dir — none of which a standalone triage CLI has. It must be mirrored, not called.
  Suggestion: Reuse only the reusable primitives (run_agent, profile selection, log_agent_result, cost extraction) directly; do not pass a synthetic CoordinatorState into run_escalation_advisor.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 2 (punt reason codes not enumerated in the spec). The plan retires it structurally — a minimal example-backed set, unknown codes rejected, unsupported discard cases routed to needs_verification, with a Step 6 test — but the chosen set will need reconciling if the report slice later ships an authoritative one.
  Suggestion: Keep the reason-code set as a single module-level constant in triage_proposal.py so a later slice can replace it in one place; the prompt should render the set from that constant rather than hardcoding it in prose.

finding_registry.description: A proposal can cite a real packet evidence id while its evidence text asserts an unrelated claim, and the parser still accepts the disposition as valid.

When a finding has checkable evidence, forge triage dispatches the normal agent runner in the project checkout with configured secrets, so the advisory stage can start CLI agents with tool access before schema validation.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
